title: Non-Atomic Read-Modify-Write (Plain Increments)
pattern: An in-place mutation (like incrementing, decrementing, or flag flipping) performed on shared mutable state from multiple threads without synchronization.
why_bad: The operation `x += 1` is not atomic; it consists of three CPU steps: read, modify, and write. Multiple threads executing these steps concurrently will interleave, resulting in lost updates and race conditions [24:210].
detection: Writing to static mut variables or shared raw pointers using mathematical assignment operators outside of atomic operations [24:210].
fix: Use atomic types with appropriate ordering invariants (`fetch_add`, `fetch_sub`) to perform lock-free state modifications safely [24:210].
